questions.prompt: What are the three main types of computer networks classified by geographical scope?
questions.answerQuote: LAN generally covers a small area, MAN a metropolitan area, and WAN a large geographical area such as a region, country or continent.

1. Introduction to Computer Networks

A computer network is a collection of interconnected devices that communicate and share resources. Devices can include computers, servers, printers, phones, switches, routers and wireless access points.

Why networks matter

• Resource sharing: files, printers, applications and internet connections can be shared.

• Communication: users and systems can exchange information.

• Centralized services: organizations can provide shared storage, authentication and applications.

• Scalability: additional devices and locations can be connected as requirements grow.

Geographical classification

• One useful classification is geographical scope. LAN generally covers a small area, MAN a metropolitan

area, and WAN a large geographical area such as a region, country or continent.

3. LAN Components and Technologies

A LAN uses networking devices and transmission technologies to connect local devices.

Common components

• Switch: connects devices on an Ethernet LAN and forwards frames toward their destinations.

• Wireless access point: provides Wi-Fi connectivity.

• Router: connects the LAN to other networks.

• Network interface: provides wired or wireless network connectivity to a device.

• Ethernet cabling: commonly provides wired LAN connections.

LAN topology

• Modern Ethernet LANs commonly use a star arrangement in which devices connect to a central switch.

Wireless LANs commonly use access points as central connection points.

4. Metropolitan Area Network (MAN)

A Metropolitan Area Network connects networks across a metropolitan or city-scale area. It is larger than a typical LAN but generally smaller than a WAN.

Characteristics

• City or metropolitan-scale coverage.

• Can connect multiple LANs.

• May use high-capacity fiber-optic links.

• Requires more extensive infrastructure than a single-site LAN.

• May be operated by an organization, service provider or partnership.

Examples

• A university connecting campuses across one city.

• A government organization connecting offices throughout a metropolitan area.

• A provider's metropolitan network linking customers and facilities.

7. WAN Devices, Services and Technologies

WAN connectivity requires systems capable of moving traffic between geographically separated networks. Routers are central because they make forwarding decisions between networks.

Common components

• Routers: forward packets between different networks.

• WAN links: communication paths connecting distant sites.

• Provider services: telecommunications providers may supply connectivity between locations.

• Firewalls and security gateways: help control traffic entering and leaving networks.

WAN approaches

• Organizations may use dedicated connectivity, provider-managed services, internet-based connections,

or combinations. The choice depends on cost, reliability, performance and security requirements.

questions.prompt: How can a large organization use LANs, MANs and WANs together?
questions.answerQuote: A large organization can use LANs at individual sites, metropolitan connectivity between nearby sites, and WAN connectivity between distant regions.

9. How LAN, MAN and WAN Work Together

These categories are not isolated. A large organization can use LANs at individual sites, metropolitan connectivity between nearby sites, and WAN connectivity between distant regions.

Example

• A university can have a LAN in each faculty building.

• A metropolitan connection can link campuses around the same city.

• A WAN can connect those campuses to a remote campus or cloud infrastructure.

• Routers connect separate networks while switches and access points provide local connectivity.

Key idea

• LAN, MAN and WAN describe different networking scales. A network can therefore be part of a larger

interconnected system.
